items.title: Live: Ley backers demoted from shadow cabinet as Taylor unveils new front bench
items.description: Angus Taylor is preparing to unveil his new-look front bench, promoting key allies and relegating backers of deposed Liberal leader Sussan Ley. Follow live.

items.title: Man who allegedly threw homemade bomb in Invasion Day rally crowd named
items.description: The man accused of throwing a bomb at Invasion Day protesters in an alleged terrorism act attack in Perth can be named as Liam Alexander Hall.

items.title: 'You make your bed, you lie in it': Albanese's warning to 'ISIS brides' in Syria
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese insists the federal government will not repatriate the Australian families with links to Islamic State fighters who remain in Syria.

items.title: Are discounts fair dinkum? Coles' 'Down Down' pricing in the spotlight
items.description: Coles downplays what shoppers understood when they saw its "Down Down" price tags, saying "not much", on the second day of a bombshell federal court case.

items.title: Police scour outhouse, water tank in Gus search
items.description: SA police have inspected an outhouse where fresh cement has recently been laid and a water tank as part of the latest search for Gus Lamont in South Australia's Mid North, with no evidence so far.

items.title: How a single Louvre ticket complaint led to the bust of a $16m scam ring
items.description: Foreign tour guides and staff who were paid to remain silent orchestrated a counterfeit ticketing ring that robbed the Louvre of millions over more than a decade, Parisian prosecutors say.

items.title: Iran launches military drill as US deploys aircraft carrier on eve of nuclear talks
items.description: Representatives from the two nations are set to meet in Geneva on Tuesday, local time, as US President Donald Trump tries to curb Tehran's nuclear program.

items.title: Third cocaine seizure brings French Polynesia haul to $2.4 billion
items.description: French authorities seized a 2.4-tonne drug shipment near French Polynesia during a joint operation with the United States.

items.title: Crews race to contain central Victorian bushfire ahead of wind change
items.description: The fire at Trawool, south of Seymour, broke out near the Goulburn Valley Highway in central Victoria on a day when half the state was facing extreme fire danger.

items.title: Fire crews battle blaze south of Launceston
items.description: The Tasmania Fire Service has downgraded an emergency bushfire warning for an area south of Launceston, with helicopters and ground crews in attendance.

items.title: 'How the hell' does Australia dominate moguls? The answer is no secret
items.description: To the surprise of many, the "beach nation" that is Australia is the best moguls skiing nation on earth. How the team got there is no accident.

items.title: 'Too shattering for language': Former ACT commissioner alleges sexual assault
items.description: Vanessa Turnbull-Roberts says she stepped down as the ACT's first Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and young people commissioner to prioritise her safety after being subjected to sexual harassment and sexual assault by a public servant.

items.title: Woman shares insight into harrowing childhood in Queensland's state care
items.description: A Queensland woman whose adolescence was marred by sexual abuse and exploitation has described her experiences in residential care to Queensland's Child Safety Commission of Inquiry.

items.title: Lunar New Year celebrations paint Australian cities red
items.description: Lion dances and red packets are on display in Sydney and Melbourne, as the cities' Asian communities ring in the Year of the Horse.

items.title: One man dead, two people critically injured in 'random' Sydney stabbing attack
items.description: Police were told on arrival at the scene in Merrylands that a man stabbed multiple people before leaving the area on foot.

items.title: Mobil agrees to pay $16 million fine for false fuel claims
items.description: The ACCC said Mobil advertised its Mobil Synergy fuel but did not actually supply the product at the time.

items.title: Couples celebrate 70 years of marriage and 70 years being neighbours
items.description: A month after Ron and June Carter got married and moved in together, his sister got married and moved in next door. This year marks not just 70 years of marriage for both couples, but 70 years of being next-door neighbours.

items.title: Rare bird spotted on outback cattle station for first time
items.description: A project with dozens of monitoring sites across the Queensland property confirms the presence of the critically endangered plains-wanderer by analysing bird calls.

items.title: Sydney man to be sentenced over 'abhorrent' 40-second rally speech
items.description: Brandan Koschel was arrested after he appeared on a stage for an open mic session during the anti-immigration March for Australia event in Sydney's Moore Park.

items.title: What is driving petrol prices down in Brisbane?
items.description: A combination of economic factors means Brisbane motorists have experienced below-average fuel prices for an extended period.

items.title: TAFE chief executive resigns as fallout over course errors widens
items.description: The number of carpentry apprentices impacted by a Charles Darwin University blunder that will force them back to school has grown to more than 130 people.

items.title: Four men again jailed for life for killing Albanian refugee in Adelaide
items.description: Four men who faced a retrial over the murder of Albanian refugee Urim Gjabri in Adelaide's north in 2018 are again jailed for life, with the judge saying their crime was motivated by "greed and [a] desire to rob him of the cannabis".

items.title: CCTV shows man on fire after firebombing of NSW convenience store
items.description: A man engulfed in flames is captured on CCTV after an arson attack at a Hunter Valley business.

items.title: Musician and former NT administrator Ted Egan remembered at state funeral
items.description: Hundreds of people have gathered to remember former NT administrator, musician and Indigenous land rights advocate Ted Egan, at a state funeral held in Alice Springs today.

items.title: 'Nobody knows how it ends': Why Australians can't turn away from US politics
items.description: Huge crowds have flocked to live shows for the popular and influential Pod Save America podcast, suggesting Australia's obsession with US politics isn't going away anytime soon.
